identity.model_type: A text-generation model for code generation.
identity.name: ReflectionCoder-DS-33B
identity.summary: ReflectionCoder is an approach that uses reflection sequences built from compiler feedback to improve one-off code generation performance.

possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: Fine-tuned on 22k reflection sequences and 156k code instruction data; no reported evaluation of factual/code correctness, so code-generation model may produce plausible but incorrect code.

possible_risks.description: In AI-assisted decision-making tasks, reliance measures how much a person trusts (and potentially acts on) a model's output. Over-reliance occurs when a person puts too much trust in a model, accepting a model's output when the model's output is likely incorrect. Under-reliance is the opposite, where the person doesn't trust the model but should.
possible_risks.justification: Open-weight code-generation model with no reported safety or correctness evaluation; users may over-trust generated code in software tasks.

possible_risks.description: Copyrighted information or other intellectual property might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.
possible_risks.justification: Code instruction tuning data may include copyrighted code snippets, and users can paste proprietary code into prompts for generation.

possible_risks.description: Confidential information might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.
possible_risks.justification: Text-generation code model accepts arbitrary user prompts; users may include confidential source code or secrets when requesting code generation.

possible_risks.description: Determining who is responsible for an AI model is challenging without good documentation and governance processes. The use of synthetic data in model development adds further complexity, since the lack of standardized frameworks for recording synthetic data design choices and verification steps makes accountability harder to establish.
possible_risks.justification: Open-weight checkpoint with Apache-2.0 license and no documentation of governance or verification of the 156k instruction/22k reflection data, making responsibility for outputs unclear.

specifications.model_size: 62.1 GiB of safetensors weights (66,679,539,760 bytes) in BF16

training_context.training_data: The target model was fine-tuned on 22k reflection sequence data and 156k code instruction tuning data, with reflection sequence datasets listed as SenseLLM/ReflectionSeq-GPT and SenseLLM/ReflectionSeq-DS.
